2027-03-03.title: Mid-Fast · Wednesday of the fourth week of the Great Fast · The Exaltation of the Cross in the middle of the Fast
readings: The Son of Man will be betrayed, killed, and raised
The bronze serpent lifted on a pole
Samuel prays at Mizpah; the people fast
O taste and see that the Lord is good
They shall look on the one whom they have pierced
No burden beyond what is necessary
The rock was Christ; God is faithful
As Moses lifted up the serpent, so must the Son of Man be lifted up
2027-03-03.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), fourth week. Mid-Fast (Pakuthi Nombu): the Panchangam names the day “the setting up of Golgotha.” At the middle of the Great Fast the Church lifts up the Holy Cross. In many parishes the Cross is set up in the middle of the church, honoured with a procession and hymns, and kept there for veneration through the rest of the Fast. Customs vary; follow your parish.
2027-03-03.verse: And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life.
theo: Today we stand at the middle of the Great Fast, and our Church does something striking: it lifts up the Cross. The Panchangam calls this day Pakuthi Nombu, Mid-Fast, and names it “the setting up of Golgotha.” In the Syriac tradition the faithful who have been walking through the Fast are shown, halfway, where the road leads: to the hill of Calvary, where the Cross will stand, and to the empty tomb beyond it. The Cross set up in the middle of the church is like a milestone and a signpost together. It tells weary travellers: you are not lost; this is where we are going; and this is what will give you strength for the rest of the way. Many of us have begun to tire. Some resolutions have already slipped. The Church does not scold; she lifts up the Cross and says: look.

The readings explain why looking is enough. In the wilderness the people grew “impatient on the way” and spoke against God and Moses, and poisonous serpents bit them. When they confessed, “We have sinned,” God did not simply remove the serpents. He told Moses: “Make a poisonous serpent, and set it on a pole; and everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live.” Jesus himself takes up this image in the Gospel: “And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life. For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life.” St John Chrysostom explained that in the wilderness the bronze image of a serpent healed bodies from the bite of real serpents, while on the Cross Christ, in the likeness of sinful flesh yet without sin, heals souls from the bite of the ancient serpent (in substance). The cure looks like the wound: the Son of God takes our curse upon himself so that we, looking at him in faith, may live.

The other readings fill out the picture. Zechariah foresees a day when God will “pour out a spirit of compassion and supplication” and the people “look on the one whom they have pierced” and mourn for him “as one mourns for an only child.” St John saw this fulfilled at Calvary. Samuel gathers Israel at Mizpah, where they fast, pour out water before the Lord, and confess, “We have sinned against the Lord,” and Samuel cries out to God for them; later he will set up a stone there and say, “Thus far the Lord has helped us.” That is a perfect Mid-Fast prayer. Paul reminds the Corinthians that their ancestors in the desert “drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ,” warns them not to put Christ to the test “as some of them did, and were destroyed by serpents,” and then encourages them: “God is faithful, and he will not let you be tested beyond your strength, but with the testing he will also provide the way out so that you may be able to endure it.” The apostles in Acts lift needless burdens from the Gentile believers, and the evening Gospel already announces the Passion and the third day. And the Psalm gives the response of the whole day: “Look to him, and be radiant; so your faces shall never be ashamed… O taste and see that the Lord is good.” We look at the Cross, and we taste the Lord's goodness in the Holy Qurbono, where the One lifted up on Golgotha gives us his Body and Blood.
conn: The bronze serpent and the Cross.
Numbers 21 and John 3:14–15: the sign lifted up in the desert points to the Son of Man lifted up on the Cross; looking in faith brings life.
Zechariah 12:10 is quoted in John 19:37 at the piercing of Jesus' side: “They will look on the one whom they have pierced.”
Thus far the Lord has helped us.
At Mizpah Israel fasts and confesses (1 Samuel 7:6); the Ebenezer stone (7:12) is a Mid-Fast milestone: God has carried us to the halfway point.
1 Corinthians 10:4 reads the desert journey as a figure of the Christian life, nourished by spiritual food and drink.
fathers: There the bronze serpent healed bodies from the bite of serpents; here the Crucified heals souls from the bite of the devil. There the image of a serpent, here the Lord in the likeness of sinful flesh, yet without sin (Homilies on John 27, in substance).
Moses' serpent teaches that we are freed from the poison of sin by looking to the mystery of the Passion, to the One who took the form of our sin (Life of Moses II, in substance).
magis: The bronze serpent was one of the images God permitted that pointed ahead to the Incarnation and the Cross.
By his Passion and death on the Cross Christ gave new meaning to suffering; it can unite us with his redemptive Passion.
The Cross is the unique sacrifice of Christ, and he calls his disciples to take up their cross and follow him.
outline: Ask: when you are tired halfway through a journey, what helps you keep going?
The bronze serpent and the Son of Man lifted up.
Point 2 · The one whom they have pierced
Mourning that heals; God so loved the world.
Point 3 · Thus far the Lord has helped us
Mizpah, the rock that is Christ, the way out.
“So must the Son of Man be lifted up.”
live: Today spend five minutes simply looking at a crucifix, at church or at home, without saying anything; then say: Lord, you did this for me.
Write down three ways God has helped you in the first half of the Fast, and one resolution you will take up again for the second half.
2027-03-03.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, at the middle of this holy Fast your Church lifts up your life-giving Cross. As the bitten Israelites looked at the bronze serpent and lived, let us look at you, lifted up for us, and live. Pour out on us the spirit of compassion and supplication, that we may look on you whom our sins have pierced and turn to you with all our hearts. Thus far you have helped us; carry us through the rest of the Fast to Golgotha and to the joy of your Resurrection. To you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, be glory for ever. Amen.
altar: The Cross set up in the church and the altar of the Holy Qurbono speak of the same Sacrifice: the One lifted up on Golgotha is offered and given to us, truly present, so that we may “taste and see that the Lord is good.”

2027-03-03.action: Spend five minutes looking at a crucifix in silence today.
2027-03-03.question: What has the Lord helped me with in the first half of the Fast, and what do I need to take up again?
term: The middle of the Great Fast, kept on the Wednesday of the fourth week. The Holy Cross is lifted up and honoured, often set up in the middle of the church as a sign of Golgotha, to strengthen the faithful for the second half of the Fast.
kidsaint: Today is the middle of the Great Fast. The Church puts up the Cross to remind us where we are walking: to Good Friday and to Easter Sunday. Lesson: when you get tired of being good, look at the Cross and remember how much Jesus loves you.

family.explain: In the desert, snakes bit the people. God told Moses to make a bronze snake and lift it up on a pole. Anyone who looked at it was healed. Jesus said he would be lifted up on the Cross like that, so that everyone who looks at him with faith will have life with God. Today, in the middle of the Great Fast, the Church lifts up the Cross for us to look at.
family.intention: We pray that our family may keep the Fast faithfully until Easter.
family.ask: Ask: “What has been hard for us in the Fast so far? What can we start again?”

illus: On a long pilgrimage walk from Thiruvananthapuram toward a shrine in the hills, a group of parishioners reached a roadside cross at midday. Someone had told them it marked the halfway point. Their feet were blistered and two of the younger men were talking about taking a bus. The old priest who walked with them asked them all to sit around the cross for a few minutes. He said: you have already done half. Look at him. He walked all the way to the end for you. They drank water, prayed one decade of the rosary, and stood up. Nobody took the bus.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, lifted up on the Cross, we look to you. Heal us and strengthen us for the rest of the Fast. Amen.
share: Everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live (Numbers 21:8). What wound do I need to bring before the Cross?
They shall look on the one whom they have pierced (Zechariah 12:10). Do I feel sorrow for my sins when I look at the crucifix?
Thus far the Lord has helped us (1 Samuel 7:12). How has God helped me in the first half of this Fast?
pm.resp: Lord, by your Cross, save us.
interc: For the whole Church at the middle of the Great Fast, that we may persevere.
For those who have given up their Lenten resolutions, that they may begin again.
For the sick and those who suffer, that they may find strength in the Cross.
For all who bear wounds of sin and addiction, that they may look to Christ and live.
For our parish, that the Cross in our midst may draw many to confession and the Holy Qurbono.
pm.close: Father, you so loved the world that you gave your only Son. As we look on him lifted up, pour out on us the spirit of compassion and supplication, keep us faithful through the testing, and bring us to the joy of Easter. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today we are halfway through the Great Fast, and the Church lifts up the Cross. The Panchangam calls this day the setting up of Golgotha. It is a signpost for tired travellers: this is where we are going, and this is what gives us strength.

In the desert the people became impatient on the way, and serpents bit them. God told Moses: make a poisonous serpent, and set it on a pole; and everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live (Numbers 21:8). The cure was simply to look, in faith.

Jesus says: just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life. For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son (John 3:14–16). Zechariah adds: they shall look on the one whom they have pierced, and mourn (Zechariah 12:10).

Paul encourages us: God is faithful, and he will not let you be tested beyond your strength (1 Corinthians 10:13). Let us say with Samuel: thus far the Lord has helped us (1 Samuel 7:12). Look at the Cross, taste the Lord's goodness at the altar, and walk on to Easter. Amen.
kids: Children, today is the middle of the Great Fast! The Church puts up a big Cross for us to see. Long ago, God told Moses to lift up a bronze snake, and everyone who looked at it got better. Jesus was lifted up on the Cross so that everyone who looks at him with love can be healed from sin. Look at the Cross today and say: thank you, Jesus.

intro: Theme: “So must the Son of Man be lifted up.”
At Mid-Fast the Church lifts up the Cross: the bronze serpent, the pierced one, and the God who has helped us thus far.

sub: The Son of Man lifted up.

And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.

They will look on the one whom they have pierced.
points.apply: Make a good confession before the Passion Week, looking at the Cross as you examine your conscience.

points.h: Thus far the Lord has helped us
sub: The way out of every testing.
q: Then Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and Jeshanah, and named it Ebenezer; for he said, “Thus far the Lord has helped us.”
God is faithful, and he will not let you be tested beyond your strength, but with the testing he will also provide the way out so that you may be able to endure it.
points.apply: Write down how God has helped you in the first half of the Fast and take up one dropped resolution again.

concl: Halfway through the Fast, the Church lifts up the Cross so that we may look and live.
The God who has helped us thus far will carry us to Golgotha and to the empty tomb.
2027-03-03.resolve: Look to the Cross every day until Easter, and finish the Fast with fresh courage.
